pr_title: Add support for VERSION field type in SQL and EQL
pr_comments: Hi @luigidellaquila, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

> There seems to be a problem with queries like select `first(version::string::version) from apps` though.

The reason for this error is that StreamOutput has no writer defined for Version type. The blocker for fixing it is that Version class is in x-pack, so I cannot reference it from inside Server module. Unfortunately I don't see a simple solution for this, apart from moving Version implementation to Server module, with all the implications on licensing. 
In my opinion, a fix with this impact (changes to multiple modules, licensing implications) is not justified by the uncommon use case, unless there is some request from the user base. My suggestion is to leave it as it is for now and track it with a new issue.

issue_context.title: EQL support for fields of type version
issue_context.body:
EQL doesn't support `version` type fields e.g. `sequence by agent.version` where `agent.version` is of type `version` fails with 

```
verification_exception: Found 1 problem\nline 2:38: Cannot use field [agent.version] with unsupported type [version]
```

The `version` field type was introduced in 7.10 https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/59773

review_comments: Curious if there's any reason not to allow a major of `0` here.

Nothing very specific, I just needed a random dataset that did not collide with my WHERE conditions. 
Looking at it now, probably it's a bit overkill to test a result set, but still it validates that the query returns correct results in a fairly randomized environment.

Giving VERSION a size of Integer.MAX_VALUE seems wrong, though I guess that's the theoretical max. Not sure if ES type enforces any limit? It seems there's only a recommendation, but no actual limit: https://semver.org/#does-semver-have-a-size-limit-on-the-version-string
Technically, any string can be indexed as a Version, so the limit is the same as a KEYWORD.
is this still needed? Shouldn't by now the runtime type always be `Version`?

It depends on how tolerant we want to be with automatic casts in situations like local folding (e.g `WHERE '1.2.0' < '1.11.0'::version`)  and function evaluation (eg. `IIF(version > '1.1', 1, 0)`).

In general, we do not do it for local folding (eg. for numbers `'2' > 1` returns `false`) but we do it for field queries (eg. `id > '3'` will evaluate to `true` even if `id` is numeric, same with `version > 1.2`). 

IMHO this is an inconsistency: the same operation should have the same behavior, locally and in _search.
Since local folding is just an optimization or a fallback in most of the cases, so I tend to consider the automatic cast as the expected behavior.

So from my point of view we should leave it as it is
I would tend to not make an exception for `Version`. Since we have this distinction between local execution and queries it should at least be consistent across types.
I don't see the usefulness of this set of data. Can you explain, please?

It was an attempt to randomize the test dataset as much as possible, adding valid and invalid version values outside of the range of the test queries so that the tests are still predictable. Eg. test that random values that do not match the test criteria are not returned by mistake.
I think you need to look at `testUnsignedLongVersionCompatibility` as a test example for `version`. What do you think @bpintea?
